key_insight: A noise-aware emulator can accurately predict the behavior of neutral-atom analog quantum processors by propagating dominant hardware imperfections through the full computation cycle.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical validation and design tool for tuning algorithms, diagnosing error sources, and improving reliability of Pasqal-style quantum hardware.
method: Model dominant microscopic noise mechanisms across the full analog workflow.
Benchmark the emulator on quantum annealing and post-quench dynamics.
Compare predictions against three Pasqal processors where classical simulation still serves as ground truth.
evidence_signal: Across all three devices, measured observables stayed within the emulator’s predicted uncertainty envelopes.
watch_item: Validation is shown only in regimes where classical ground truth is still available, so performance in classically intractable settings remains to be demonstrated.
paper_title: Noise-aware emulation and cross-device validation of neutral atom analog quantum processing units
